item.title: WSPHA maintain operation despite dry spell
item.description: The West Sepik Provincial Health Authority (WSPHA) is continuing its full operations despite the prolonged dry season affecting the province and other parts of the country. While several schools and health centers nationwide have scaled down operations due to water shortages, WSPHA Chief Executive Officer Stanley Masi says Vanimo General Hospital is not affected.
item.content:encoded:
The West Sepik Provincial Health Authority (WSPHA) is continuing its full operations despite the prolonged dry season affecting the province and other parts of the country.

While several schools and health centers nationwide have scaled down operations due to water shortages, WSPHA Chief Executive Officer Stanley Masi says Vanimo General Hospital is not affected.

Mr. Masi told NBC News the hospital has a water bore well source that supplies water for toilets, laundry and general cleaning, while rainwater tanks are used for drinking water for both patients and staff.

Meanwhile, CEO Masi confirmed the Authority is yet to receive any El Nino funding from the National Department of Health, the National Government or the Sandaun Provincial Government to support rural health facilities.

"For us in Vanimo, the hospital is doing fine. Our main concern is Telefomin, which is now experiencing severe drought and water shortage. Other centers affected, include Nuku, Aitape and Lumi who are now scaling down on some of its services," Mr. Masi said.

The National Government has released El Nino funds to provincial and district administrations to support essential services like health and education, Mr. Masi hopes the PHA will receive a portion to support its district hospitals and health centers.

Mr. Masi added that it is time the National Government funds PHAs directly, rather than channeling funds through the National Department of Health.

item.title: Assembly calls for proper reporting
item.description: ‎Divisional and Departmental heads within the Milne Bay Provincial Administration in Milne Bay Province, have been urged to provide timely reports on major activities in the province. ‎ ‎This call was made by Acting Chairman and Deputy Governor, Mathew Magioudi, during the province's assembly meeting on Friday following concerns over the lack of activity reports from some government divisions. ‎ ‎
item.content:encoded:
‎Divisional and Departmental heads within the Milne Bay Provincial Administration in Milne Bay Province, have been urged to provide timely reports on major activities in the province. ‎ ‎This call was made by Acting Chairman and Deputy Governor, Mathew Magioudi, during the province's assembly meeting on Friday following concerns over the lack of activity reports from some government divisions. ‎ ‎During a session of questions without notice, a supplementary question was raised in the assembly regarding Timber and logging operations in the province, including it's licenses and permits, the benefits they are bringing to the people of Milne Bay.

However, no detailed report was presented as Chairman responsible for forestry did not have any report at hand to answer the series of questions. ‎ ‎This prompted the Acting Chairman and Deputy Governor, Mathew Magioudi, who sternly called on the Provincial Administration to immediately look into addressing the failure by some departmental and divisional heads in providing accurate and detailed reports to respective chairmen in the Provincial Assembly. ‎ ‎"It is very frustrating to see that the divisional heads and certain department managers have not been working together with their chairman's. Non-compliant to PEC and assembly requirements are very bad", The acting Chairman said ‎ ‎"I wish to call upon and put on record in this assembly; the administrator of various departments responsible must take seriously the concerns and the welfare of the people of Milne Bay Province" ‎ ‎The acting Chairman advised the provincial administration that the Assembly is the only forum through which the public gets to hear and learn about what the government is doing for them as other communication mediums are not effective in remote areas. ‎ ‎He stressed that proper and timely reporting is therefore very essential for accountability and transparency, adding that a lack of accurate information from divisional and departmental heads makes it difficult for the provincial assembly to effectively scrutinize government activities, funded programs and the impact it has on communities.

‎He added that respective advisors in the provincial administration must understand that providing reports is part of their responsibility to the Provincial Government and the general public.

item.title: Garaina tea is premium quality world market standard
item.description: Wau Waria’s Garaina tea has been confirmed to be a top organic premium quality tea, that can generate about K20 million to K30 million annually and compete on the world market. In a recent consultation workshop, International Tea Specialist, Gayal Perera described Garaina Tea as a premium product with the quality and growing conditions required to compete internationally, strengthening the economi
item.content:encoded:
Wau Waria’s Garaina tea has been confirmed to be a top organic premium quality tea, that can generate about K20 million to K30 million annually and compete on the world market.

In a recent consultation workshop, International Tea Specialist, Gayal Perera described Garaina Tea as a premium product with the quality and growing conditions required to compete internationally, strengthening the economic case for rehabilitating the long-dormant plantation.

Perera, a Sri Lankan tea specialist and Eco metric Limited partner, has visited Garaina twice in recent weeks to inspect the plantation area and assess its production and market potential.

He specialises across the 'Field to Export' tea value chain from growing and processing, through to packaging and getting the finished product onto market shelves.

“The estimated long-term tea production potential is about 600 to 620 tons per year. Upon inspections, I’m confident to say that Garaina tea is a high value, single origin PNG tea with progressive organic certification, it is top premium quality with the potential to compete on the world market,” Perera said.

Under a proposed 400-hectare state land, Garaina has the potential to produce an estimated 600 to 620 metric tons of premium tea annually.

Monitoring and evaluation expert and adviser to the Department of National Planning and Monitoring, Wilco Liebregts, gave an estimate that 600 tonnes of premium-quality tea produced from the 400 hectares could generate between K20 million and K30 million every year, depending on the market.

“Six hundred tons of premium quality tea grown on 400 hectares could bring in about K20 million to K30 million a year, based on the lows and highs in prices, but the nucleus estate has to be commercially viable and profitable so that it can stand on its own feet,” he said.

Liebregts was also part of the team involved in the drafting of the Medium-Term Development Plan 4 (MTDP4) in which Garaina Tea was featured.

He also referred to an Asian Development Bank (ADB) study assessing small and medium enterprises, potentially worthy of support, saying Garaina Tea was highly regarded in that assessment and so, the economic opportunity extends beyond the tea itself.

The MP, Marsh Narewec said the objective to bring the key players together, was not simply to reopen an old plantation, it is to establish a commercially sustainable industry around a premium agricultural product that was once enjoyed by the Queen of England.

“The purpose of bringing all you key stakeholders together is to present, share constructive ideas together and agree on how we can partner to get this project off the ground."

“The World Bank and donor partners may come with funding, but they will require counterpart funding from us. We cannot entirely depend on development partners to fund everything,” Narewec said.

He said his DDA will start off with Phase One of the project and expect other stakeholders to step in as part beneficiaries of this important project.

In response, the DAL Policy and Dialogue Adviser, Robyn Ekstrom welcomed the collaborative approach, saying DAL is pleased to be part of the initiative and is prepared to support the district’s efforts to revive the historic tea project.

item.title: Holy Trinity short of teachers despite getting 10 TSC positions
item.description: Sixty-one students of Holy Trinity Humanities Academy in Baro, West Coast Vanimo, are sitting their Grade 10 National Examinations for the first time as pioneers. The new Junior High School was established under the 1-6-6 reform to give West Coast children access to proper education.
item.content:encoded:
Sixty-one students of Holy Trinity Humanities Academy in Baro, West Coast Vanimo, are sitting their Grade 10 National Examinations for the first time as pioneers.

The new Junior High School was established under the 1-6-6 reform to give West Coast children access to proper education.

However, as these students prepare to move into Grade 11 next year, the school is facing teacher shortage.

Rector Fr. Christopher Etheridge said the school was inspected in 2024 by Senior Secondary Inspector Ben Suming, who recommended it be registered as a Level 9 school to offer Grades 7 to 10 by 2025 and Grades 11 to 12 by 2026 to 2027, with 32 teaching positions.

He said the school was registered as a church agency school in 2024/2025 but only received its school code and 10 TSC positions this year.

"We registered and are recognized as a church agency school. Our registration came in 2024. But only this year did we receive our school code and 10 of the 32 positions requested. We are still struggling to get the other 22 positions," Fr. Etheridge said.

Fr. Etheridge said for the first two years the school survived on borrowed positions, parental project fees and overseas donations, and only started receiving Government Tuition Fee Subsidy (GTFS) in Term 2 this year. Two teachers are still on borrowed positions.

He said the main challenge is not advertising, but having enough positions to recruit.

"It is hard to recruit teachers for Grades 7 to 11 when you only have 10 positions to work with. We had to email, visit Moresby and constantly call officials just to get the 10 we have now," he said.

He acknowledged teachers who took the risk to join the school early, including Mr. Gregory Rere who left St. Ignatius to join them in 2025.

As a Humanities Academy, the school is in need of qualified teachers in English, Literature, History and Arts, including music teachers for its Queen of Paradise Orchestra program.

Fr. Etheridge said all teachers must be TSC registered and said the school has been emailing TSC in Port Moresby weekly for the past two months with no response. He however thanked local inspectors Mr. Waino and Mr. Alieng for their support.

He is appealing for passionate teachers to join the Academy.

"We want teachers who are passionate about teaching, who want to make an impact by teaching the truth and showing love. If you want to teach in an environment rooted in love of God, love of truth and love of teaching, give us a call," he said.

Interested teachers can apply via email at holytrinityschool@ive.org with an interest letter, CV and contact details.

item.title: Lam, Bai and Johnston out
item.description: The PNG Rugby Football League released the PNG Kumuls squad for the 2026 Rugby League World Cup today with several notable omissions. Leigh Leopards halfback Lachlan Lam (wrist surgery), Gold Coast Titans Cooper Bai (hamstring) and Alex Johnston (rib) have all been ruled out of the 23-men squad.
item.content:encoded:
The PNG Rugby Football League released the PNG Kumuls squad for the 2026 Rugby League World Cup today with several notable omissions.

Leigh Leopards halfback Lachlan Lam (wrist surgery), Gold Coast Titans Cooper Bai (hamstring) and Alex Johnston (rib) have all been ruled out of the 23-men squad.

Adding to the 23 players, three have been selected as shadow players.

The Kumuls squad will feature several new faces in camp with Josh Feledy from Manly Sea Eagles, Luca Moretti from Parramatta Eels and New Zealand Warriors bound Bailey Biondo Odo.

Earlier this year Feledy made his intentions known about representing the birth place of his grand father and mother, and he will finally tick that box when he runs out with the Kumuls.

Moretti is eligible to play for the Kumuls through his mother, who was born in PNG, while Odo has PNG heritage through his father.

Incumbent Kumuls captain Rhyse who has played 21 Tests for the country has been named, and he is likely to lead the Kumuls possibly for his last World Cup.

Nene Macdonald, who played three games for St Helens this season is also named, adding experience to camp along with Leigh Leopards duo Edwin Ipape and Liam Horne.

Following a successful season in the Hostplus Cup, Central Queensland Capras players; Valentine Richard, Nixon Putt, Zev John, Roderick Tai and Khaiya Waiembi have been rewarded and will join the Kumuls camp.

Cowboys duo Zac Laybutt and Robert Derby are familiar faces in camp, along with Townsville Blackhawks speedster Dudley Dotoi.

The 2026 Betfred Champions London Broncos have six players listed with Epel Kapinias, Gairo Voro, Morea Morea, Finley Glare, Robert Mathias and Alex Max (Shadow player) except for Jeremiah Simbiken (knee).

PNG Hunters Sylvester Namo and Sanny Wabo have also been named, following their recent outing in the Prime Ministers XIII, with Newcastle’s Jacob Taulani (Shadow).

Veteran Kyle Laybutt is still playing third tier football in Queensland and got the call up as a shadow player.

item.title: First Western Highlander surrender illegal firearm
item.description: A Western Highlander has made the decision to give up the firearm he kept for his own protection for the past three years. Jason Yaim, a local SME owner from the Jika tribe in Hagen Central, today (071026) became the first person in Western Highlands to formally surrender an illegal firearm under the current gun amnesty program.
item.content:encoded:
A Western Highlander has made the decision to give up the firearm he kept for his own protection for the past three years.

Jason Yaim, a local SME owner from the Jika tribe in Hagen Central, today (071026) became the first person in Western Highlands to formally surrender an illegal firearm under the current gun amnesty program.

Yaim handed over one pistol, several rounds of ammunition, an M16 magazine and 5.56 ammunition to police at the Mt Hagen Police Station.

The handover was witnessed and received by Acting Western Highlands Provincial Police Commander Senior Inspector Steven Philipo, Eastern End Command Gun Amnesty Coordinator Inspector Maureen Undaba and other senior police officers.

"Today (071026) Jason is the first Western Highlands man to surrender his illegal firearm to the police. He made the decision yesterday at his residence at Gomis but today he brought it formally to the police station and surrendered his one pistol and several ammunitions including a m16 magazine," Philipo said.

Philipo thanked Yaim for taking the initiative, saying his decision should encourage other people who are keeping illegal firearms to come forward.

He said the gun amnesty program has already been launched across Western Highlands in partnership with the provincial government and the province's 316 ward councilors.

Philipo is also thanking the National Government for extending the deadline for people to surrender illegal firearms until December.

He elaborated the final stage of the surrender and awareness program will be held at Queen’s Park from November 25th to 26th.

" While the deadline for the gun amnesty program for Western Highlands is being extended, police will continue to carry put the gum amnesty awareness and surrender in the 11 LLGs of Western Highlands and will wrap up the final lag of the program at the Queens Park".

He says he kept the firearm because he believed it would protect him, his family and his property.

But after being convinced by a police officer, he decided it was time to surrender the weapon.

" Officer Felix came and talked me into surrendering my firearm and ammuninations. I made the decision and I am happy that at least my actions can serve as an encouragement to other Western Highlanders," Jason Yaim stressed.

Yaim's name will now be recorded as the first Western Highlander to surrender an illegal firearm under the current amnesty program.

But after giving up what he considered his means of protection, Yaim has one important question for police.

He wants to know whether police can now guarantee the safety of people who surrender their firearms and leave themselves without a weapon for protection.

" Now I want to put an appeal forward to the police and the government to guarantee the safety of those of us who have surrendered our firearms and ammunition which we have held in our procession as our guarantee of safety of our lived and properties," Yaim appealed.

Yaim's decision is now being used by police as an example for other firearm holders in Western Highlands that illegal guns can be surrendered without waiting for the amnesty period to end.

Police are urging people who are still holding illegal firearms and ammunition to follow Yaim's example and hand them over to authorities.

item.title: PM trips scrutiny
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has undertaken more than 10 international engagements this year , with concerns raised over the cost of these travels. Critics allege these trips will have cost the country millions of kinas.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape has undertaken more than 10 international engagements this year , with concerns raised over the cost of these travels.

Critics allege these trips will have cost the country millions of kinas.

These engagements began in Switzerland in January, where the Prime Minister attended the World Econimic Forum in Davos, then onto United Arab Emirates for the World Government Summit in Dubai.

In May , Mr Marape flew to France and held bilateral talks with President Emmanuel Macron and then to China for economic and bilateral dicussions in Guangdong Province.

A number of trips followed in July , which included the Annual Leaders Dialogue in Indonesia and Japan for the Pacific Islands Leaders meeting.

The Prime Minister also visited its closest partner Australia for the PNG Australia Annual Leaders Dialogue and related economic and sports engagements - trips of which continued to August.

Back in the region , Mr Marape travelled on two seperate occasions to the Solomon Islands, as part of his official state visit and also the inaugural PNG-Solomon Islands Investment summit.

He also participated in Vanuatu's 41st independence anniversary when he traveled across in July and Palau for the 55th Pacific Islands Leaders meeting.

A week after attending the United Nations General Assembly in New York , the Prime Minister was off to Tuvalu for Pre - COP 31 , ahead of the conference in Türkiye, next month.

While critics and Opposition leaders have expressed concerns on how millions in tax payers funds are being spent on these trips , which they say do not produce positive outcomes, they are demanding independent audits.

He says as the head of government these overseas engagements are necessary for the country to secure bilateral , trade and investment for the country.

"These are necessary visits that at the head of Government level, we need to attend.

"Those visits enable relationship within two Nations to flourish," PM Marape said.

item.title: Ume grateful for support following pro-bout in New Zealand
item.description: Papua New Guinea’s professional boxer John Ume is grateful for the support he has received from the Sanctuary Hotel and Rapopo Plantation Resort during his recent bout. This follows after Ume claimed the BX-9 Welterweight Championship title in New Zealand over the weekend.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea’s professional boxer John Ume is grateful for the support he has received from the Sanctuary Hotel and Rapopo Plantation Resort during his recent bout.

This follows after Ume claimed the BX-9 Welterweight Championship title in New Zealand over the weekend.

The two-time boxing Olympian turned professional boxer John Ume has dominated his recent bout in Aotearoa, New Zealand claiming the BX-9 interim Welterweight Championship.

Nicknamed ‘The Ring Monster’, Ume returned into the country early this week after going up against New Zealand’s Hemza Perwaisy.

He said his recent tour overseas was made possible after receiving a massive boost from The Sanctuary Hotel and Rapopo Plantation Resort.

“On behalf of my family, my team, and my coaches, I want to say thank you to Chief James Pang and Sanctuary and Rapopo for supporting me for my finals fight. Without their help, I wouldn't make it to this fight.”

“I'm so glad and humbled to say thank you to the staff. As you know, we won the recent fight event in New Zealand to claim the Welterweight Interim title and we’re going to keep it here until next year,” Ume said.

Ume’s recent win was through a Technical Knock-Out after seven rounds in the ring. The fight was also streamed as a live simulcast via NBC TV and Radio.

Meanwhile Sanctuary Hotel’s part-owner Chief James Pang said it was humbling to watch a young talent dominate the ring over weekend knowing, they had made the right decision to back a champion who’s continues to put PNG on the world map.

Sanctuary came on board to support after coming across a John’s social media post reaching out for sponsorship.

“We proud to have sponsored John Ume and that was well before his fight last Saturday in New Zealand, which he won impressively.

“I'm no expert on boxing, but I can see that John was in control throughout rounds up to round seven. In the seventh round, John attacked his opponent and knocked him down and for that we’re really proud of his achievement.”

Pang also affirmed that they will continue to support John Ume in his pro-boxing journey.

Meanwhile Ume has confirmed he returns to training in two weeks-time with more preparations ahead of another big fight in the next few months

item.title: No power if water at 20 percent
item.description: The El Nino induced dry weather conditions has brought water levels at the Sirinumu dam to a critical low at 53 per cent and it continuous to go down at 10 per cent every 10 days.

item.title: El Nino funds in Simbu sent directly to districts
item.description: The Simbu Provincial Disaster Office has clarified that the K2.5 million El Nino Relief Funding from the National Government has been remitted directly into all District Development Authority (DDA) accounts.
